name: Levi W. Hancock
role: Early missionary and a president of the Seventy
dateNote: He was baptized on 16 November 1830 and called to Missouri by section 52 in June 1831.
importance: Section 52 sends him with Zebedee Coltrin to Missouri, preaching on the way. His later autobiography is a key account of the June 1831 conference behind that section. He marched with Zion’s Camp in 1834 and became one of the presidents of the Seventy in 1835. Section 124 confirms him in that role as “Levi Hancock”.
connections: He traveled with Zebedee Coltrin and later served with Joseph Young among the Seventy’s presidents. He was the only general authority in the Mormon Battalion.

sources.title: Levi Ward Hancock, Joseph Smith Papers

reviewNote: Birth, death (10 June 1882, Washington, Utah), baptism, 1831 mission, Zion’s Camp, Seventy, and Mormon Battalion checked on JSP. The 124:138 “Levi Hancock” is taken to be him, consistent with his Seventy role; the batch listed only section 52.
